section_summary: This section follows preparations for the 1937 Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition through its opening and an “America Day” celebration. It contains exhibition plans and exhibitor instructions, U.S. correspondence about publicity and participation, reports on efforts to recruit Latin American exhibitors, and accounts of the ceremonies. The section ends with the beginning of a Nagoya Chamber of Commerce booklet.

subfiles.title: Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition prospectus and directions to exhibitors
subfiles.about: Sets out the exhibition program and practical terms for foreign exhibitors.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages describe the exhibition’s purposes, dates, halls and projected spending. They specify space rents, shipping and packing rules, transport discounts, customs treatment, insurance, removal permits and estimated display costs.

subfiles.title: Poster publicity letter to the Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Encloses an exhibition grounds poster and requests publicity.
subfiles.summary: Carr sends a colored grounds poster and asks Treasury to publicize it.

subfiles.title: Poster publicity letter to the Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Encloses two exhibition grounds posters and requests publicity.
subfiles.summary: Carr sends two grounds posters and asks Commerce to publicize them.

subfiles.title: Poster publicity letter to the Secretary of the Interior
subfiles.about: Encloses two exhibition grounds posters and requests publicity.
subfiles.summary: Carr sends two grounds posters and asks Interior to publicize them.

subfiles.title: Poster publicity letter to the Secretary of Labor
subfiles.about: Encloses two exhibition grounds posters and requests publicity.
subfiles.summary: Carr sends two grounds posters and asks Labor to publicize them.

subfiles.title: Poster publicity letter to the Secretary of Agriculture
subfiles.about: Encloses two exhibition grounds posters and requests publicity.
subfiles.summary: Carr sends two grounds posters and asks Agriculture to publicize them.

subfiles.title: Agriculture Department acknowledgement of posters
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt and forwards the posters for possible publicity use.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture sends the posters to its Division of Exhibits.

subfiles.title: Treasury Department acknowledgement of poster
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the poster and promises to display it.
subfiles.summary: Treasury will put the exhibition poster on a department bulletin board.

subfiles.title: Interior Department acknowledgement of posters
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the posters and promises appropriate publicity.
subfiles.summary: Interior agrees to arrange publicity for the exhibition posters.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on Nagoya’s renewed participation request
subfiles.about: Reports the Nagoya mayor’s renewed appeal for American participation.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards the mayor’s request for official U.S. participation or another way to secure broad American involvement, together with his reply.

subfiles.title: Mayor Oiwa’s letter seeking American participation
subfiles.about: Renews a request for U.S. participation in the Nagoya exhibition.
subfiles.summary: Oiwa cites Nagoya’s trade with the United States and the exhibition’s peace and cultural aims. He asks Grew to reconsider government participation or help secure substantial participation by other Americans.

subfiles.title: Grew’s reply to Mayor Oiwa
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the mayor’s request and promises to forward it to Washington.
subfiles.summary: Grew says the embassy will send Oiwa’s letter to Washington for consideration.

subfiles.title: Plan of the Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition Ground
subfiles.about: Maps and indexes the planned exhibition grounds.
subfiles.summary: The plan locates gates, halls, foreign exhibit areas, amenities, transport lines, canals and the Peace Tower. Pages 97–98 contain mostly map markings; pages 99–100 carry the title and directory.

subfiles.title: The Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition News, No. 2
subfiles.about: Reports preparations, projected exhibits and international responses.
subfiles.summary: The newsletter describes outreach to foreign governments and firms, plans for halls and transport, and ambassadors invited as honorary counsellors. It outlines displays on science, natural resources, education and sports, and illustrates Nagoya scenery and factories.

subfiles.title: Directions to Exhibitors
subfiles.about: Provides application, freight, display and cost instructions for exhibitors.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet covers applications, exhibition space rents, shipment deadlines, packing, freight discounts, customs exemptions, insurance, removal permits and construction costs. It gives a rough estimate for special halls and ends with an appeal to overseas visitors to attend the exhibition.

subfiles.title: Nagoya Consulate despatch transmitting exhibition literature
subfiles.about: Transmits new exhibition literature and reports American inquiries.
subfiles.summary: Stephan sends the exhibitor pamphlet, grounds plan and newsletter. He notes a local newspaper report that cities in the United States and Central America had inquired about participation.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on official U.S. participation
subfiles.about: Reiterates that official U.S. participation is unavailable without a Japanese government invitation.
subfiles.summary: Phillips reiterates the barrier to official participation and mentions Commerce Department inquiries into private American interest.

subfiles.title: Exhibition literature letter to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards consular exhibition literature for circulation to potential exhibitors.
subfiles.summary: Carr asks Treasury to disseminate the enclosed exhibition materials.

subfiles.title: Exhibition literature letter to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards multiple sets of exhibition literature for circulation.
subfiles.summary: Carr asks Commerce to distribute eight sets to interested associations or industries.

subfiles.title: Exhibition literature letter to Labor
subfiles.about: Forwards exhibition literature for circulation to interested groups.
subfiles.summary: Carr asks Labor to share the enclosed consular report and exhibition materials.

subfiles.title: Exhibition literature letter to Interior
subfiles.about: Forwards exhibition literature for circulation to interested groups.
subfiles.summary: Carr asks Interior to disseminate the enclosed materials to possible exhibitors.

subfiles.title: Exhibition literature letter to Agriculture
subfiles.about: Forwards exhibition literature for circulation to interested groups.
subfiles.summary: Carr asks Agriculture to disseminate the enclosed materials to possible exhibitors.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgement of exhibition literature
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the June 20 letter and exhibition materials.
subfiles.summary: Treasury thanks State for the consular despatch and exhibition literature.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgement of exhibition literature
subfiles.about: Promises to make exhibition pamphlets available to interested contacts.
subfiles.summary: Commerce will share the pamphlets with interested contacts.

subfiles.title: Agriculture acknowledgement of exhibition literature
subfiles.about: Acknowledges exhibition materials and offers appropriate publicity.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture agrees to publicize the materials as circumstances warrant.

subfiles.title: Interior acknowledgement of exhibition literature
subfiles.about: Promises to disseminate exhibition information.
subfiles.summary: Interior agrees to circulate the pamphlets and grounds plan and publicize the exhibition.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to El Salvador despatch
subfiles.about: Points to Corrigan’s report on K. Itoh’s efforts in El Salvador.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a despatch about Itoh’s exhibition promotion at Diario de Hoy.

subfiles.title: Corrigan despatch on exhibition promotion in El Salvador
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese efforts to attract Salvadoran visitors and exhibitors.
subfiles.summary: Corrigan forwards a newspaper account of Itoh’s visit. He regards claims about transport facilities, coffee sales and Japanese purchases as evidence of Japan’s effort to expand relations with El Salvador.

subfiles.title: Translation of Diario de Hoy article on Itoh’s visit
subfiles.about: Describes Itoh’s appeal for Salvadoran attendance and participation.
subfiles.summary: The article recounts Itoh’s visit with Japanese diplomat Otani, his travels to recruit Latin American participation and promised travel concessions. It also presents claims about a growing Japanese market for Salvadoran coffee.

subfiles.title: Confirmation copy of Colombia participation despatch
subfiles.about: Reports Itoh’s invitation to Colombia and his commercial arguments.
subfiles.summary: Greene reports that Itoh sought Colombian exhibits and described Nagoya’s port project and potential Japanese demand for coffee. Colombia had not announced an official decision. This is a damaged confirmation copy of the despatch appearing again on pages 138–140.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Philippine participation legislation
subfiles.about: Points to a War Department letter on Philippine participation legislation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references an act authorizing Philippine participation in the Nagoya exposition.

subfiles.title: Colombia participation despatch
subfiles.about: Reports Itoh’s invitation to Colombia and his case for Colombian exhibits.
subfiles.summary: Greene reports Itoh’s arrival in Bogotá as the Nagoya mayor’s special representative. Itoh promoted Colombian commercial representation and Japanese coffee demand and discussed transferring exhibits from a forthcoming Barranquilla fair; Colombia had not announced a decision.

subfiles.title: Second cross-reference to Philippine participation legislation
subfiles.about: Repeats the reference to Philippine participation legislation.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate note points to the War Department letter on Philippine participation.

subfiles.title: Colombia declines exhibition invitation
subfiles.about: Reports Colombia’s refusal to participate officially.
subfiles.summary: Dawson says Colombia declined because producers were unprepared and trade relations with Japan were unsettled. A federation reportedly considered sending a delegate without government sanction.

subfiles.title: Damaged report on proposed Colombian exhibit
subfiles.about: Discusses a proposed Colombian pavilion and private organizing efforts.
subfiles.summary: The damaged text mentions a Colombian federation organizing an exhibit and a proposed pavilion at Nagoya.

subfiles.title: Opening of the Nagoya Pan-Pacific Peace Exhibition
subfiles.about: Reports the exhibition’s opening ceremony, banquet and initial condition.
subfiles.summary: Stephan describes the March 14 ceremony before Prince Higashikuni, Japanese officials and foreign representatives, followed by a banquet, and records speeches emphasizing peace and international exchange. He gives exhibitor and building counts, observes that some exhibits were unfinished, and notes private American exhibits, a circus troupe and a San Francisco model.

subfiles.title: “America Day” at the Nagoya exhibition
subfiles.about: Reports ceremonies honoring visiting members of the Japan-America Society.
subfiles.summary: Stephan describes the April 24 reception, exhibition visit and dinner for Tokyo visitors. He reproduces the chamber president’s welcome and Consul Tower’s response on Ambassador Grew’s behalf, and notes American city exhibits and an enclosed booklet on Nagoya.

subfiles.title: Facts, Figures and Features of Nagoya, 1937: cover and city map
subfiles.from: Nagoya Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Introduces a booklet on Nagoya with a city map.
subfiles.summary: A consular cover identifies the enclosed chamber booklet; its opening pages contain the title and a city map.

subfiles.title: Stray copy of Colombia despatch closing page
subfiles.about: Duplicates the signature page of Greene’s Colombia report.
subfiles.summary: A copy of the despatch closing on page 140 appears amid the booklet pages.

subfiles.title: Facts, Figures and Features of Nagoya, 1937: location and history
subfiles.from: Nagoya Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Shows Nagoya’s regional location and begins its history.
subfiles.summary: A regional map and opening text describe Nagoya’s location, size and past.
